source_text: Ecclesiae quidem ueritate epistolam istam ad Ephesios habemus emissam, non ad Laodicenos; sed Marcion et titulum aliquando interpolare gestit, quasi et in isto diligentissimus explorator. nihil autem de titulis interest, cum ad omnes apostolus scripserit dum ad quosdam, certe tamen eum deum praedicans in Christo, cui competunt quae praedicantur. cui ergo competet secundum boni existimationem, quam proposuerit in sacramento uoluntatis suae, in dispensationem adimpletionis temporum — ut ita dixerim, sicut uerbum illud in Graeco sonat — recapitulare — id est ad initium redigere uel ab initio recensere — omnia in Christum, quae in caelis et quae in terrisnisi cuius erunt omnia ab initio, etiam ipsum initium, a quo et tempora et temporum adimple(tio et adimple)tionis dispensatio, ob quam omnia ad initium recensentur in Christo? alterius autem dei quod initium, id est unde, cuius opus nullum? quae tempora sine initio? quae adimpletio sine temporibus? quae dispensatio sine adimpletione? denique quid in terris egit iam olim, ut longa aliqua temporum adimplendorum dispensatio reputetur ad recensenda omnia in Christo, etiam quae in caelis? nec in caelis autem res ab altero actas existimabimus, quaecumque sunt, quam ab eo, a quo et in terris actas omnibus constat. quodsi non capit alterius <omnia) ista deputari ab initio quam creatoris, quis credet ab alio ea recenseri in Christum alium, et non a suo auctore et in suum Christum? si creatoris sunt, diuersa sint necesse est a diuerso deo; si diuersa, utique contraria. quomodo ergo contraria recenseantur in eum, a quo denique destruuntur? nam et sequentia quem renuntiant Christum, cum dicit: ut simus in laudem gloriae (eius) nos, qui praesperauimus in Christum? qui enim praesperasse potuerunt, id est ante sperasse in deum quam uenisset, nisi Iudaei, quibus Christus praenuntiabatur ab initio? qui ergo praenuntiabatur, ille et praesperabatur. atque adeo hoc ad se, id est ad Iudaeos, refert, ut distinctionem faciat conuersus ad nationes: in quo et uos, cum audissetis sermonem ueritatis, euangelium, in quo credidistis et signati estis spiritu promissionis eius sancto. cuius promissionis? factae per Iohelem: in nouissimis diebus effundam de meo spiritu in omnem carnem, id est et in nationes. ita (et) spiritus et euangelium in eo erit Christo, qui praesperabatur, dum praedicabatur. Sed et 'pater gloriae' ille est, cuius Christus rex gloriae canitur in psalmo ascendens: quis est iste rex gloriae? dominus uirtutum ipse est rex gloriae; ab illo 'spiritus sapientiae' optatur, apud quem haec quoque spiritalium species enumeratur inter septem spiritus per Esaiam; ille dabit (inluminatos cordis oculos', qui etiam exteriores oculos luce ditauit, cui displicet caecitas populi: et quis caecus nisi pueri mei? et excaecati sunt famuli dei; apud illum sunt et 'diuitiae hereditatis in sanctis'. qui eam hereditatem ex uocatione nationum repromisit: postula de me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditatem tuam; ille 'inoperatus est in Christum ualentiam suam suscitando eum a mortuis et collocando eum ad dexteram suam subiciendo omnia', qui et dixit: sede ad dexteram meam, donec ponam inimicos tuos scabellum pedum tuorum; quia et alibi spiritus ad patrem de filio: omnia subiecisti sub pedibus eius. si ex his alius deus et alius Christus infertur, quae recognoscuntur in creatore, quaeramus iam creatorem. plane, puto, inuenimus, cum dicit illos delictis mortuos, [non] in quibus ingressi erant secundum aeuum mundi huius, secundum principem potestatis aeris, qui operatur in filiis incredulitatis. sed mundum non potest et hic pro deo mundi Marcion interpretari. non enim simile est creatum creatori, factum factori, mundus deo. sed nec princeps potestatis aeris dicetur qui est princeps potestatis saeculorum. numquam enim praeses superiorum de inferioribus notatur, licet et inferiora ipsi deputentur. sed nec incredulitatis operator uideri potest, quam ipse potius et a Iudaeis et a nationibus patitur. sufficit igitur, si haec non cadunt in creatorem. si autem et est, in quem magis competant, utique magis hoc apostolus sciit. quis iste? sine dubio ille, qui ipsi creatori filios incredulitatis obstruit, aere isto potitus, sicut dicere eum propheta refert: ponam in nubibus thronum meum: ero similis altissimo. hic erit diabolus, quem et alibi, si tamen ita et apostolum legi uolunt, deum aeui huius agnoscemus. ita enim totum saeculum mendacio diuinitatis impleuit. qui plane si non fuisset, tunc haec in creatorem spectasse potuissent. sed et (si) in Iudaismo conuersatus fuerat apostolus, non quia interposuit de delictis: in quibus et nos omnes conuersati sumus, ideo delictorum dominum et principem aeris huius creatorem praestat intellegi, sed quia in Iudaismo unus fuerat de filiis incredulitatis diabolum habens operatorem, cum persequeretur ecclesiam et Christum creatoris, propter quod et: incredulitatis fuimus, inquit. sed natura, ne, quia filios appellauit Iudaeos creator, argumentetur haereticus dominum irae creatorem. cum enim dicit: fuimus natura filii iracundiae creatoris autem non natura sunt filii Iudaei, sed adlectione patrum, irae filios ad naturam retulit, non ad creatorem. ad summam subiungens: sicut et ceteri, qui utique filii dei non sunt, apparet communi naturae omnium hominum et delicta et concupiscentias carnis et incredulitatem et iracundiam reputans, diabolo tamen captante naturam, quam et ipse iam (in)fecit delicti semine inlato. Ipsius, inquit, sumus factura, conditi in Christo. aliud est enim facere, aliud condere. sed utrumque uni dedit. homo autem factura creatoris est: idem ergo condidit in Christo, qui et fecit. quantum enim ad substantiam, fecit, quantum ad gratiam, condidit. Inspice et cohaerentia: memores uos, aliquando nationes in carne, qui appellamini praeputiatio ab ea quae dicitur circumcisio in carne manu facta, quod essetis illo in tempore sine Christo, alienati a conuersatione Israhelis et peregrini testamentorum et promissionis eorum spem non habentes et sine deo in mundo. sine quo autem deo fuerunt nationes et sine quo Christo? utique eo, cuius erat conuersatio Israhelis et testamenta et promissio. at nunc, inquit, in Christo uos, qui eratis longe, facti estis prope in sanguine eius. a quibus erant retro longe? a quibus supra dicit: a Christo creatoris, a conuersatione Israhelis, a testamentis, a spe promissionis, a deo ipso. si haec ita sunt, ergo his prope fiunt nunc nationes in Christo, a quibus tunc longe fuerunt. si autem conuersationi Israhelis, quae est in religione dei creatoris, et testamentis et promissioni et ipsi deo eorum proximi sumus facti in Christo, ridiculum satis, si nos alterius dei Christus de longinquo admouit creatori. meminerat apostolus ita praedicatum de nationum uocatione ex longinquo uocandarum: qui longe erant a me adpropinquauerunt iustitiae meae. tam enim iustitia quam et pax creatoris in Christo adnuntiabatur, ut saepe iam ostendimus. itaque ipse est, inquit, pax nostra, qui fecit duo unum — Iudaicum scilicet et gentile, quod prope et quod longe — soluto medio pariete inimicitiae in carne sua. sed Marcion abstulit (sua), ut inimicitiae daret 'carne', quasi carnali uitio [non J Christo aemulae. sicubi alibi dixi, et hic, non Marrucine, sed Pontice: cuius supra sanguinem confessus es, hic negas carnem? Si legem praeceptorum sententiis uacuam fecit, — adimplendo certe legem; uacat enim iam: non adulterabis, cum dicitur: (nec uidebis ad concupiscendum', uacat: non occides, cum dicitur: (nec maledices); aduersarium legis de adiutore non potes facere — ut duos conderet in semetipso — qui fecerat idem condens, secundum quod et supra: ipsius enim factura sumus conditi in Christo — in unum nouum hominem, faciens pacem — si uere nouum, uere et hominem, non phantasma, nouum autem, ut noue natum ex uirgine dei spiritu — ut reconciliet ambos deo — et deo, quem utrumque genus offenderat, et Iudaicum et gentile — in uno corpore, inquit, cum inter fecisset inimicitiam in eo per crucem: ita et hic caro corpus in Christo, quod crucem pati potuit. hoc itaque adnuntiante pacem eis qui prope et eis qui longe, accessum consecuti simul ad patrem iam non sumus peregrini et aduenae, sed conciues sanctorum, sed domestici dei, — utique eius, a quo supra ostendimus alienos fuisse nos et longe constitutos — superaedificati super fundamentum apostolorum. abstulit haereticus: et prophetarum, oblitus dominum posuisse in ecclesia sicut apostolos ita et prophetas, si non timuit, ne et super ueterum prophetarum fundamentum aedificatio nostra constaret in Christo, cum ipse apostolus ubique nos de prophetis exstruere non cesset unde enim accepit summum angularem dicere Christum, nisi de psalmi significatione: lapis, quem reprobauerunt aedificantes, iste factus est in summo anguli?
pass_a_gloss: Indeed we have the truth of the Church that this letter was sent to the Ephesians, not to the Laodiceans; but Marcion also sometimes endeavors to interpolate the title, as if he were a very diligent investigator in this matter. However, the titles are of no concern, since the apostle wrote to all, while writing to certain ones, certainly preaching God in Christ, to whom belong the things that are preached. To whom, therefore, will it belong, according to the good estimation that he proposed in the sacrament of his will, in the dispensation of the fulfillment of times - so to speak, just as that word sounds in Greek - to recapitulate, that is, to reduce to the beginning or to recount from the beginning, all things in Christ, which are in heaven and which are on earth, if not to him whose are all things from the beginning, even the beginning itself, from which are also the times and the dispensation of the fulfillment of times, on account of which all things are recounted in Christ? What beginning, that is, from where, does another god have, whose work is none? What times without a beginning? What fulfillment without times? What dispensation without fulfillment? Finally, what has he done on earth, so that a long dispensation of fulfilling times may be reckoned to recount all things in Christ, even those in heaven? Nor, indeed, will we consider that the things that are done in heaven are from another than from him, from whom it is evident that all things done on earth are. If these things cannot be assigned to another from the beginning, except to the Creator, who will believe that they are recounted in another Christ, and not by his own author and in his own Christ? If they are the Creator's, they must necessarily be different from those of another god; if different, certainly contrary. How, therefore, can contrary things be recounted in him, from whom they are finally destroyed? For also the following words declare Christ, when he says: so that we may be to the praise of his glory, we who have hoped in Christ. For who could have hoped before, that is, hoped in God before he came, except the Jews, to whom Christ was proclaimed from the beginning? He, therefore, who was proclaimed, was also hoped for. And so this refers to them, that is, to the Jews, so that he makes a distinction, turning to the nations: in which also you, when you heard the word of truth, the gospel, in which you believed and were sealed with the Holy Spirit of his promise. Whose promise? The one made through Joel: in the last days I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh, that is, also on the nations. Thus, both the Spirit and the gospel will be in Christ, who was hoped for, while being preached. But also 'the Father of glory' is he, whose Christ, the King of glory, is sung in the psalm, ascending: who is this King of glory? The Lord of hosts, he is the King of glory; from him the 'Spirit of wisdom' is sought, with whom also these species of spiritual things are enumerated among the seven spirits through Isaiah; he will give 'enlightened eyes of the heart', who also enriched the outer eyes with light, to whom the blindness of the people is displeasing: and who is blind, if not my children? And they were blinded, the servants of God; with him are also 'the riches of the inheritance in the saints'. He promised this inheritance from the calling of the nations: ask of me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance; he 'worked in Christ, raising him from the dead and placing him at his right hand, subjecting all things', who also said: sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet; because also elsewhere the Spirit says to the Father about the Son: all things have been subjected under his feet. If from these things another god and another Christ are inferred, which are recognized in the Creator, let us seek the Creator now. Indeed, I think we have found him, when he says that those who are dead in sins, not in those in which they entered according to the age of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, who works in the sons of disobedience. But the world cannot be interpreted for the god of the world by Marcion. For the created is not like the Creator, the made is not like the Maker, the world is not like God. But neither can the prince of the power of the air be said to be the prince of the power of the ages. For never is the ruler of superior things noted from inferior things, although inferior things are also assigned to him. But neither can the operator of disobedience be seen, which he himself rather suffers from both the Jews and the nations. It is sufficient, therefore, if these things do not fall to the Creator. But if they are, in whom they may belong more, certainly the apostle knew this better. Who is this? Without doubt, he who obstructs the sons of disobedience to the Creator himself, having been possessed by that air, just as the prophet says: I will set my throne in the clouds; I will be like the Most High. This will be the devil, whom also elsewhere, if indeed one wants to read the apostle in this way, we recognize as the god of this age. For thus the whole age has been filled with the lie of divinity. Who, indeed, if he had not been, then these things could have been directed towards the Creator. But also if the apostle had been living among the Jews, not because he interposed concerning sins, in which we all have lived, therefore the Lord of sins and the prince of the air is shown to be the Creator, but because in Judaism he was one of the sons of disobedience, having the devil as operator, when he persecuted the Church and Christ of the Creator, on account of which he also says: we were of disobedience. But by nature, lest, because the Creator called the Jews sons, the heretic argues that the Lord of wrath is the Creator. For when he says: we were by nature sons of wrath, the sons of the Creator are not by nature, but by adoption, he referred the sons of wrath to nature, not to the Creator. Adding in summary: just as also the others, who certainly are not sons of God, it appears that he reckons the common nature of all men, and the sins and the desires of the flesh and the disobedience and the wrath, considering that nature is taken captive by the devil, which he also has already corrupted with the seed of sin. For he says: we are his work, created in Christ. For it is one thing to make, another to create. But he gave both to one. Man, however, is the work of the Creator: therefore, he also created in Christ, who made. As much as regards substance, he made; as much as regards grace, he created. Consider also the coherence: you were once Gentiles in the flesh, who are called uncircumcision by that which is called circumcision in the flesh made by hand, because you were at that time without Christ, alienated from the conversation of Israel and strangers to the covenants and the promise of them, having no hope and without God in the world. Without which God, however, were the nations, and without which Christ? Certainly, the one whose conversation was that of Israel, and the covenants, and the promise. But now, he says, you who were far off have been made near in the blood of Christ. From whom were you far off? From whom he says above: from Christ of the Creator, from the conversation of Israel, from the covenants, from the hope of the promise, from God himself. If these things are so, therefore, the nations are now made near in Christ, from whom they were far off. But if we have been made near to the conversation of Israel, which is in the religion of the God of the Creator, and to the covenants and the promise and to God himself, it is ridiculous enough, if the Christ of another God has brought us near from afar to the Creator. The apostle remembered that he had preached thus about the calling of the nations from afar: those who were far from me have come near to my righteousness. For both the righteousness and the peace of the Creator were announced in Christ, as we have often shown. Therefore, he himself is our peace, who made the two one - namely, the Jewish and the Gentile, which is near and which is far - having abolished the middle wall of enmity in his flesh. But Marcion removed his own, so that he might give 'flesh' to enmities, as if to a carnal vice, not to Christ. As I said elsewhere, and here, not in a Marrucine, but in a Pontic sense: to whom you confessed above, whose blood you now deny, the flesh? If he made the law of commandments empty by fulfilling it - for it is now empty: you shall not commit adultery, when it is said: you shall not look at someone to lust; it is empty: you shall not kill, when it is said: you shall not speak evil - you cannot make the adversary of the law from the helper - so that he might create two in himself - who made the same, creating - according to what is also said above: for we are his work, created in Christ - into one new man, making peace - if truly new, truly also a man, not a phantom, new, however, as born anew from the virgin by the Spirit of God - so that he might reconcile both to God - and to God, whom both the Jewish and the Gentile people had offended - in one body, he says, when he made enmity in it through the cross: thus also here the flesh is the body in Christ, which was able to suffer the cross. Announcing peace, therefore, to those who are near and to those who are far, we have obtained access simultaneously to the Father, and we are no longer strangers and foreigners, but fellow citizens of the saints, and members of God's household - certainly of him, from whom we were shown above to be alienated and constituted far off - built upon the foundation of the apostles. The heretic removed: and the prophets, having forgotten that the Lord placed in the Church both apostles and prophets, if he did not fear that our building might also be established on the foundation of the old prophets in Christ, since the apostle himself everywhere ceaselessly builds us up from the prophets, whence did he receive the saying that Christ is the chief cornerstone, if not from the signification of the psalm: the stone that the builders rejected, this has become the chief cornerstone?

bible_refs.note: in nouissimis diebus effundam de meo spiritu in omnem carnem

pass_b_english: The Church's truth is clear: this letter was sent to the Ephesians, not the Laodiceans. Marcion, however, tries to alter the title, acting like a diligent investigator. But titles don't matter, since the apostle wrote to all people, preaching God in Christ, who owns everything being preached. So, who deserves to bring all things together in Christ, as proposed in God's will, in the plan to fulfill all times (Ephesians 1:10)? This means reducing everything to its starting point or recounting it from the beginning - all things in heaven and on earth. If not the one who owns all things from the start, including the beginning itself, then who? The one from whom all times and their fulfillment originate, making all things count in Christ. What beginning does another god have, with no work to show? What times exist without a starting point? What fulfillment happens without times? What plan is there without fulfillment? What has this other god done on earth to deserve a long plan for fulfilling times, making all things count in Christ, even in heaven? We won't assume things done in heaven come from a different god than the one responsible for everything on earth. If these things can't be assigned to another god from the start, except the Creator, who would believe they're recounted in another Christ, not by their original author and in their own Christ? If they belong to the Creator, they must differ from those of another god; if different, they're opposing. How can opposing things be brought together in Christ, who ultimately destroys them? The following words also declare Christ: we will be to the praise of God's glory, we who have hoped in Christ (Psalm 24:10). Who could have hoped in God before Christ came, except the Jews, to whom Christ was proclaimed from the beginning? The one proclaimed was also hoped for. This refers to the Jews, making a distinction when turning to the nations: you, who heard the word of truth, the gospel, believed and were sealed with the Holy Spirit of the promise made through Joel (Joel 2:28). Both the Spirit and the gospel will be in Christ, who was hoped for while being preached. The Father of glory is the one whose Christ, the King of glory, is sung in the psalm, ascending. The Lord of hosts is the King of glory, from whom the Spirit of wisdom is sought, as enumerated in Isaiah (Isaiah 11:2). He gives enlightened eyes of the heart and enriched outer eyes with light, displeased by the people's blindness. The servants of God were blinded. With him are the riches of the inheritance in the saints. He promised this inheritance from the calling of the nations: ask of me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance. He worked in Christ, raising him from the dead, placing him at his right hand, and subjecting all things. If these things imply another god and Christ, recognized in the Creator, let's seek the Creator. We've found him, saying those dead in sins aren't in the state they entered according to this world's age, following the prince of the air's power, who works in disobedient people. But the world can't be interpreted as the god of the world by Marcion. The created isn't like the Creator; the made isn't like the Maker; the world isn't like God. The prince of the air's power can't be the prince of the ages' power. The ruler of superior things isn't noted from inferior things, though inferior things are assigned to him. The operator of disobedience isn't seen, which God rather suffers from both Jews and nations. It's sufficient if these things don't apply to the Creator. If they do, the apostle knew better. Who is this? The devil, obstructing disobedient people to the Creator, having that air, as the prophet says. This devil is recognized as the god of this age, filling it with the lie of divinity. If he hadn't existed, these things could have been directed towards the Creator. The apostle lived among Jews, not because he interposed concerning sins, but because he was one of the disobedient, having the devil as operator, persecuting the Church and Christ of the Creator. By nature, the Creator's sons aren't naturally sons, but adopted, referring sons of wrath to nature, not the Creator. The apostle adds that all people share a common nature, sins, desires, disobedience, and wrath, with nature taken captive by the devil, corrupted by sin. We are his work, created in Christ, made and created by the same God. Consider: you were once Gentiles, without Christ, alienated from Israel's conversation, strangers to covenants, without hope, and without God. Which God were you without, and which Christ? The one whose conversation was Israel's, with covenants and promises. Now, you've been made near in Christ's blood, from whom you were far off - from Christ, Israel's conversation, covenants, promises, and God. If we've been made near to Israel's conversation, covenants, promises, and God, it's ridiculous if another God's Christ brought us near to the Creator. The apostle preached that those far off have come near to God's righteousness. Both righteousness and peace were announced in Christ, as shown before. He is our peace, making Jews and Gentiles one, abolishing the middle wall of enmity in his flesh. Marcion removed this, giving 'flesh' to enmities, not to Christ. If he fulfilled the law, making it empty, he can't be the law's adversary. He created two in himself, making one new man in Christ, reconciling all to God, in one body, through the cross. We've obtained access to the Father, no longer strangers, but fellow citizens of saints, members of God's household, built on the apostles' foundation. The heretic removed the prophets, forgetting the Lord placed both apostles and prophets in the Church, fearing our building might be established on the old prophets' foundation in Christ. The apostle received the saying that Christ is the chief cornerstone from the psalm, which says the stone rejected by builders became the chief cornerstone.

review.notes: Pass B fails on scripture citations and accuracy. 1. Pass B cites (Psalm 24:10) for 'we will be to the praise of God's glory, we who have hoped in Christ', but the Latin 'ut simus in laudem gloriae (eius) nos, qui praesperauimus in Christum' is a paraphrase of Ephesians 1:12, not Psalm 24:10. 2. Pass B cites (Isaiah 11:2) for 'Spirit of wisdom', but the Latin 'spiritus sapientiae' is a general reference/gloss; while Isaiah 11:2 contains the term, the translation fails to maintain the distinction between the text and the citation. 3. Pass B cites (Joel 2:28) for 'the promise made through Joel', which is acceptable, but the mismatch in the Psalm citation is a definitive error. 4. Pass B omits the specific nuance of 'recapitulare' as 'reducing to the beginning' in its summary of the mechanism, though it captures the essence.
reasons: Pass B provides a wrong citation for the clause 'ut simus in laudem gloriae (eius) nos, qui praesperauimus in Christum' by attributing it to (Psalm 24:10) instead of the actual context (Ephesians 1:12).
